note.text: With S assumed nonempty, A implies I and E implies O: these downward inferences are subalternation. Falsity travels upward from I to A and O to E. A false universal does not determine its contrary, and a true particular does not establish its corresponding universal. Undetermined means the supplied information permits either truth value; it does not mean false. If S can be empty, use the standard meanings directly and retain only the contradictory diagonals without extra existence information.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to use opposition and subalternation while distinguishing false from undetermined. Builds on: categorical meanings and opposition relations. Leads to: guided square problems and eduction.

sections.heading: Read the original model
sections.text: Original model: if some club members have badges, I is true. That alone leaves A undetermined: all members might have badges, or some might not. If A is true and members exist, I is true. In a complete counted model, inspect both regions: {2} members inside P and {1} outside P make A false, E false, I true and O true.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: State the existence convention, identify the given form and truth value, then use only a licensed direction. Test an uncertain case by describing alternatives. Counts supplied as a complete model can settle more than a single square premise.
